title: Trinidadian Corn Soup
description: Split peas cooked to nothing, thickened with coconut milk, and loaded with corn on the cob and hand-rolled dumplings. Street food that gets made in a drum on a Saturday night.
notes: The split peas have to collapse completely before anything else goes in. Half-cooked peas never catch up, and the soup stays thin around them.

steps.text: Simmer the yellow split peas in the water with the thyme until they have lost their shape entirely.
steps.tip: Skim the grey foam in the first five minutes. It never dissolves and it dulls the finished pot.

steps.text: Soften the onion, garlic, and carrots in the coconut oil, then tip the lot into the peas.
Add the corn on the cob rounds and lower the scotch bonnet in whole, and simmer until the corn gives to a fork.
steps.tip: Unpierced, the pepper perfumes the pot and nothing more. Burst it and the whole batch belongs to it.

steps.text: Pour in the coconut milk and bring it back to a bare simmer, then season with the salt.
Rub the plain flour and fine salt together and add just enough of the warm water to make a stiff dough.
Rest the dough, then roll teaspoons of it between your palms into short tapered cigars.
Drop the dumplings into the simmering soup and cook them until they float and are no longer floury in the middle.
Fish the scotch bonnet out before you serve, and put the corn rounds in the bowls first so everybody gets one.
